results.explanation: At DeleteSpaceMember entry, the supplied premise gives a successful resolveSpaceMemberResource result. The handler obtains the authenticated current user, target user, caller membership, and target membership, then computes isSelf from the target and current-user IDs. Under the other-member premise, isSelf is false, so the visible non-self authorization branch invokes requireSpaceAdministrator(callerMembership). The supplied principal is an ordinary non-administrator, so this control denies before the deletion call. The accepted policy expectation is allow, because an active ordinary member may remove a different active member of the same space without administrator authority; therefore the observed source-visible denial does not match the accepted policy. The DeleteSpaceMember store call and subsequent SSE publication are the later effect path, and are not reached on this denied branch.

entry.statement: DeleteSpaceMember requires the current user before resolving the requested member resource.

binding.statement: The handler compares the resolved target user ID with the authenticated current user ID to determine whether the request is self-directed.
The resolved resource supplies the target user, caller membership, and target membership used by the handler.

control.statement: When the target is not the caller, the handler requires space administrator authority and returns the error if that check fails.

effect.statement: If authorization passes, the handler would delete the resolved membership and publish a space-changed event; on this denied path those later effects are not reached.

condition.statement: The supplied other-member premise makes the target different from the caller, so the non-self administrator check executes.

results.explanation: At DeleteSpaceMember entry, the supplied premise gives a successful resolveSpaceMemberResource result. The handler obtains the authenticated current user and resolved membership data, then computes isSelf from the target and current-user IDs. Under the self-leave premise, isSelf is true, so the non-self administrator check is skipped. Control proceeds to the Store.DeleteSpaceMember call and, if that mutation returns no error, publishes the space-changed event and returns success. The accepted policy expectation is allow, because an active ordinary member may delete their own membership; the observed source-visible authorization result matches that expectation. The store deletion and event publication are effects after the authorization control, not themselves the authorization check.
